composition.story: K-means groups points by repeating two moves. Each point joins its nearest centroid. Each centroid then moves to the mean of its points. Watch six points on a line until no point switches. Total squared distance only falls, then stops.

aha.observation: No point switched clusters, so the centroids stopped moving. Each assign or update step only lowered total squared distance, until it stopped at 9.33.

controls.label: Step
controls.presentation: Previous and Next buttons; the rail shows the active step

controls.label: Starting centroids
controls.presentation: Selects the variant. Changes the start, so the first rounds differ. Both end at the same clusters.

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Returns to step 1 and the default start

states.label: Place centroids
states.sentence: Choose k=2 and drop two starting centroids on the line. No point has a cluster yet.

states.label: Assign
states.sentence: Every point joins its nearest centroid, measured by distance on the line.
states.why: Point 4 sits on centroid 2, so it joins cluster 2.

states.label: Update
states.sentence: Each centroid moves to the mean of its cluster. The big cluster pulls centroid 2 far right.
states.why: Centroid 2 has the farthest to travel.

states.label: Reassign
states.sentence: With the centroids moved, nearest-centroid is checked again. One point changes its mind.
states.why: Point 4 is now closer to centroid 1.

states.label: Update again
states.sentence: Both centroids move again to the means of their new clusters. The moves are smaller now.
states.why: Both centroids land at the center of three points.

states.label: Converged
states.sentence: Checking nearest centroids once more, nothing switches. The centroids would not move, so the algorithm stops.

states.label: Place centroids
states.sentence: Choose k=2 and drop two starting centroids close together on the left. No point has a cluster yet.
states.why: Both centroids start crowded at the left end.

states.label: Assign
states.sentence: Every point joins its nearest centroid. Centroid 2 captures almost everything.
states.why: Point 4 is closer to centroid 2 than to centroid 1.

states.label: Update
states.sentence: Each centroid moves to the mean of its cluster. Centroid 2 is dragged to the middle of the line.
states.why: Centroid 1 stays put because it owns one point.

states.label: Reassign
states.sentence: With the centroids moved, nearest-centroid is checked again. Two points change clusters.
states.why: Point 4 is now closer to centroid 1.

states.label: Update again
states.sentence: Both centroids move again to the means of their new clusters, reaching the same spots as the other start.
states.why: Same clusters give the same means.

states.label: Converged
states.sentence: Checking nearest centroids once more, nothing switches. The centroids would not move, so the algorithm stops.
